newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-APIs seen neutral, though gasoline surprises.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-APIs seen neutral, though gasoline surprises.

text.p: The weekly American Petroleum Institute inventory report Wednesday should have little effect on NYMEX futures prices, market players said, though the draw in gasoline stocks raised some eyebrows.
"I don't think it means much," said Thomas Blakeslee, trader with Cargill Investor Services. "The only thing that was a surprise was the gasoline drawdown."
Most of the weekly stock figures were within the range of analysts' estimates, rendering the report neutral, traders said, while gasoline attracted some late support buying.
During after-hours ACCESS trading on NYMEX, March gasoline dipped slightly, March heating oil shed nearly 0.50 cent and March crude oil dipped about 15 cents.

Gasoline stocks fell 1.269 million barrels for the latest reporting week, despite analysts' call for a build of 1.125 million barrels. "I think demand was underestimated last week," said Tom Bentz, director of the energy division at ING Derivatives Clearing Inc "We did see weaker than expected demand in the past couple of reports," Blakeslee added.

Strong demand appeared to be evident in the current statistics, which showed a draw in total stocks despite a jump in output to 7.287 million barrels per day, up 244,000 bpd from the previous week. Imports dipped by a modest 81,000 bpd from a week ago.

The API figures showed a build in crude stocks of 3.122 million barrels for the week ended February 14, with the 7.05-million barrel build in Gulf Coast levels far outpacing the 4 million barrel draw on the West Coast.
The drop in crude inventories was slightly puzzling, traders said, since imports fell and refinery runs increased.
The API also revised up the week-ago report's crude totals by about 2.3 million barrels.

Distillate stocks slipped 2.897 million barrels, with the key East Coast's high sulphur distillate, or heating oil, levels accounting for about 1.6 million barrels of that figure. "That draw in the heating oil was right on" with seasonal expectations, according to a spot products trader.

Spot distillate barrels saw little action in the wake of the report, after suffering a pounding on differentials across the board earlier in the day amid unseasonably balmy weather in the Midwest and key Northeast market.

But news of the gasoline draw helped flush out some buying interest late in the afternoon. "It stimulated gas just a little." Refinery utilization increased 0.7 of a percentage point to 88.3 percent of capacity, mostly due to refineries returning units to service after seasonal maintenance.
